title: GIFT: Geometry-Induced Functional Transfer for Category-level Object Manipulation
why: The closest missing mechanism: it transfers object-centric interaction functions and geometric constraints from one demonstration across substantially different shapes using functional maps and geometry-aware paths. It is the primary prior against any claim that geometry-induced functional transfer itself is new.

title: Pointing-VLA: Typed Spatial Grounding Interfaces for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
why: A very recent VLA threat that exposes object-functional grounding, next-stage points, and visual trajectories through typed spatial heads. It directly tests whether an explicit functional-geometry interface already handles the proposed geometry-conditioned stage changes.

title: LiLo-VLA: Compositional Long-Horizon Manipulation via Linked Object-Centric Policies
why: It targets tasks with multiple kinematic-structure changes and zero-shot long-horizon composition through linked object-centric interaction policies and dynamic replanning. This is a load-bearing sequence-composition baseline for geometry changes that alter intermediate relation events.

title: Action with Visual Primitives
why: AVP makes the VLM emit a next-stage target and visual-primitive tokens for the action expert, with spatial-compositional generalization. It is a current comparator for whether stage-level visual primitives already adapt approach, grasp, and placement behavior without an explicit skill-graph-shift model.

title: GEAR-VLA: Learning Geometry-Aware Action Representations for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
why: The strongest recent generic geometry-aware VLA baseline, combining discrete embodied reasoning, semantic-aligned 3D integration, and embodiment-canonical actions. It defines the boundary the new direction must exceed rather than relabeling ordinary 3D/action-representation robustness as functional-geometry adaptation.

title: MATCH POLICY: A Simple Pipeline from Point Cloud Registration to Manipulation Policies
why: It represents manipulation as a sequence of relative poses and transfers demonstrations to unseen geometries by registering pick/place targets. This is a direct older baseline for claims about geometry-dependent keyframes, grasps, and insertion strategies.

title: Shelving, Stacking, Hanging: Relational Pose Diffusion for Multi-modal Rearrangement
why: RPDiff is the canonical relational-geometry baseline for multi-modal object-scene placement across novel shapes, poses, and layouts. Its endpoint-pose focus is precisely the nearest prior that a geometry-induced intermediate-strategy benchmark must separate from.

title: RoboTwin 2.0: A Scalable Data Generator and Benchmark with Strong Domain Randomization for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
why: It supplies current executable simulation infrastructure, manipulation-relevant object annotations, automated task code, and many bimanual tasks. It is the most useful missing benchmark backbone for constructing controlled geometry substitutions, although its published randomization is broader than the requested fixed-language/fixed-terminal-relation intervention.
